brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.requirement: A planter of four cells (four planting cells with soil)
requirements.evidence: There are 4 drained third-depth bins (bin:0..3,0,0~hex-bin-third-drain), each filled with soil and planted (prop:1-4).

requirements.requirement: Four cells / bases in the planter
requirements.evidence: There are 4 full hex bases: piece:0,0,0, 1,0,0, 2,0,0 and 3,0,0.

requirements.requirement: A water pipe running through the bases
requirements.evidence: run:run-1 (irrigation mode) starts at the west face of (0,0) and goes straight through (1,0), (2,0) and (3,0).

requirements.requirement: The pipe feeds every one of the four cells
requirements.evidence: The run passes under the bin in every one of the four cells. The configurator doesn't model emitters, how water reaches the soil, leaks or flow, so whether each cell is actually watered can't be checked here.

finish.summary: I built a planter of four full hex bases in a straight row, cells (0,0) to (3,0). One irrigation pipe run (run-1) comes in through the open west face of (0,0) and goes straight through all four bases. Because the run passes through each cell, only shallow third-depth bins fit there, so each base holds a drained third-depth bin filled with soil and planted with a seedling. I capped the open edges, except where the pipe enters, and bolted the joints. check_build found no rule issues and no mesh clashes. The configurator lists the run as a non-potable irrigation supply. It doesn't model emitters, how water gets from the pipe into each bin, leaks or flow, so whether every cell actually gets water can't be checked here. Print estimate: 29 printed parts, about 1813 g.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
